title: arXiv mathematics — daily notable papers, 30 October 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart. The checked Semantic Scholar records had zero citations for these new papers, and exact-title searches mainly surfaced arXiv records or automated mirrors rather than independent expert discussion; attention evidence is therefore limited.

sections.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
sections.abstract: The authors count tropical matching fields and hyperplane-sequence types, derive first-order asymptotics for regular triangulations of products of simplices, and compare the order-type expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three mathematical classifications connect combinatorial enumeration, tropical/algebraic geometry, and optimization; the abstract states a first-order asymptotic answering a question of Santos.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed rank parameter r, the relevant counts grow as n^((r−1)^2 n+o(n)); this yields the same asymptotic for regular triangulations of Δ^(n−1)×Δ^(r−1), answering Santos's question. The authors also compare real and signed-tropical order types and show a collapse for the parity-game double-tropicalization class.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: As n tends to infinity with r fixed; structures include max-plus tropical hyperplane sequences, coherent matching fields, and associated labeled order types.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline enumeration is first-order asymptotic rather than an exact count, and its implications concern structural expressivity, not a direct algorithmic complexity improvement.

sections.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
sections.abstract: The author proves a conformal scaling limit from a Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear combinatorial disks to a random flat surface prescribed by a path-integral formulation of JT gravity, and gives an exploration-based convergence criterion.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Probability and mathematical physics cross-listing, a proved scaling limit for a specified disk ensemble, and a general criterion based on branching explorations make this a bridge between discrete random geometry and continuum gravity.
sections.claimed_result: After rescaling as the distinguished base length tends to infinity, the critical Boltzmann rectilinear disk converges in law to a flat JT-gravity surface; the conformal factor converges on compact subsets under the stated uniformization. The paper also gives a criterion for other discrete models.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The explicit model is a critical Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear disks with a long distinguished side. The general criterion requires an exploration with a Markov property, tightness, and joint convergence of the length process and associated data.
sections.unique_caveat: The criterion does not establish convergence for every proposed disk model; those applications still require the exploration and tightness hypotheses. The construction also uses a conformal-welding theorem from a companion paper.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of the 2D Euler Evolutions with L¹∩Lᵖ Vorticity
sections.abstract: For every fixed 1<p<∞, the authors construct compactly supported L¹∩Lᵖ initial vorticity for which the unforced two-dimensional Euler equation has two distinct, exactly transported Lagrangian evolutions on [0,1].
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a precise nonuniqueness result while retaining strong continuity, exact vorticity transport, and regular Lagrangian flows; the authors describe a detailed multiscale construction.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct two distinct evolutions from the same limiting datum by cascading unstable four-vortex configurations across scales, with a difference persisting at positive time and detectable by a smooth observable.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced 2D incompressible Euler on [0,1]; for each prescribed finite p>1, the compactly supported initial vorticity lies in L¹(R²)∩Lᵖ(R²), and both evolutions are strongly continuous there and transported by their own measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction parameters and initial datum may depend on p, so the result does not supply one datum working simultaneously for every p. The claim is a new preprint result and warrants expert scrutiny.

sections.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
sections.abstract: The authors prove global well-posedness near a Maxwellian in bounded C³ domains for the Landau equation with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions, including Coulomb interactions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It states global existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence in a bounded-domain kinetic PDE setting, including the Coulomb case; the 98-page manuscript indicates a technically extensive proof, not external validation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim global strong solutions from small compatible Gaussian perturbations and uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions for −3≤γ≤1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Perturbations are small and compatible with a Maxwellian; the spatial domain is bounded and C³, with either in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is perturbative and tied to the stated boundary and regularity assumptions; the abstract does not assert large-data well-posedness.

sections.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
sections.abstract: For a squarefree-supported Rademacher random multiplicative function, the authors prove an almost-sure two-sided law of the iterated logarithm for its partial sums when normalized by the full predictable quadratic variation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result links probability and number theory and gives an explicit almost-sure limit and cluster set for a classical random multiplicative model; the abstract also isolates a further unresolved fluctuation alternative.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove limsup and liminf equal to +1 and −1 after normalization by √(2Q(x)log log x), with the same result using log log Q(x), and identify the normalized cluster set as [−1,1].
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f is a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on squarefree integers; M(x) is its partial sum and Q(x) is the full predictable quadratic variation of the prime-revealing martingale.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors leave open which of two alternatives holds for the limsup normalized instead by √x(log log x)^(1/4): a finite positive nondegenerate random variable or infinity almost surely.

sections.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
sections.abstract: The author proves bigraded strong formality for compact hyperkähler manifolds and develops algebraic formality tools for multicomplexes and commutative n-differential graded algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three mathematical categories meet in a stated formality theorem for all compact hyperkähler manifolds; the abstract also describes a generalized ∂∂̄-lemma and an algebraic theorem supporting the geometric claim.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes that compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, and proves an algebraic formality theorem for the stated multicomplex setting.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The geometric statement is for compact hyperkähler manifolds and the specified pluripotential-homotopy notion of bigraded strong formality; the algebraic framework uses objects with multiple differentials.
sections.unique_caveat: The claim concerns this particular strong-formality notion and homotopy-theoretic setting; it should not be read as an unrestricted equivalence of all invariants with those of compact Kähler manifolds.

sections.title: Singular value decompositions over *-algebras with applications to tensor decompositions
sections.abstract: The authors characterize finite-dimensional *-algebras admitting singular value decompositions and extend SVD-based low-rank tensor formats, with quasi-optimality guarantees depending on commutativity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines an algebraic characterization, an explicit ordered-SVD algorithm, and tensor-decomposition guarantees; its applications make the abstract method computationally testable.
sections.claimed_result: The authors characterize which finite-dimensional *-algebras K admit an SVD for every matrix and which inner products yield Eckart–Young optimality. They claim TT-SVD remains quasi-optimal for every such K, while HOSVD, ST-HOSVD, and TTN-SVD retain that guarantee when K is commutative.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Matrices and tensors are over a finite-dimensional *-algebra with the specified compatible inner products; the stated stronger tensor guarantees depend on whether the algebra is commutative.
sections.unique_caveat: The quasi-optimality result is not uniform across all tensor formats and algebras; the abstract's empirical compression examples do not establish lower error for every data set.
